rulingTitle: If an ordinary run receives the canonical ID but emits a different value in run.start data.runId, this test still passes.

action.reason: Real test-coverage gap: the AC-1 test stops at runSetupPhase and only asserts the runId passed in, never the run.start data.runId emitted at run-setup-init.ts:202. Production passes the runId straight through, so the risk is test strength only; fix needs a harness running real setup and capturing the log line, suitable for branch review.

rationale: Verified by reading the test and run-setup-init.ts: finding is accurate, but it is test-only with no known production defect, and the story hit its fix-round cap.

rulingTitle: O_NOFOLLOW protects only the final component: after resolution, replacing an intermediate directory with an escaping symlink reproducibly makes readLogTextNoFollow return outside content.

action.reason: Exploiting this needs write access to the user's own output directory tree, which already lets an attacker replace the log file directly. Static escaping symlinks are handled at resolution (AC-15), and the read is read-only and same-user, so the residual TOCTOU is not worth an openat-style rewrite.

rationale: Hardening of an already-confined path whose threat model requires equivalent local privilege; the spec's required behaviours are met.

rulingTitle: When O_NOFOLLOW rejects a target swapped after discovery, ELOOP escapes runReplay before metrics/status loading; replay crashes instead of degrading to available artifacts.

action.reason: The crash only occurs if a log is swapped for a symlink or non-regular file between discovery and read. Replay fails closed with no foreign content read, and missing, invalid or escaping logs at discovery already degrade to metrics/status. A try/catch returning [] in readJsonlLenient is a cheap follow-up.

rationale: Narrow race, fail-closed and safe, with no data exposure; worth a follow-up but not blocking.
